prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a continuous bright-to-dark floor gradient across an indoor sports hall, placing the near court floor at 1–2 m and fading to the curved back wall and elevated balcony above at over 15–20 m. In frames 3 and 5, a bright foreground silhouette at the bottom edge (roughly 0.5–0.8 m away) shows the head of a badminton racket held within the camera wearer's arm's reach, partly cropped at the lower boundary, whereas it is completely omitted in frames 1, 2, and 4 despite being visible in RGB. Across the mid-ground (roughly 7–14 m away), a badminton net post stands left of centre at about 7–9 m while four distant players—two on the left side of the net (roughly 10–14 m away, 2–4 m apart) and two on the right (roughly 9–12 m away)—appear as medium-grey silhouettes that move closer together on the right side until their silhouettes overlap in frames 2–5. The map clarifies the continuous 3D ground plane and relative depth ordering between the near net post, the players behind it, and the recessed background wall more clearly than RGB alone. However, it is unreliable for thin and translucent structures: the badminton net mesh is treated as a solid wedge attached to the post, the foreground racket in frame 1 is completely missed, and the hollow racket head in frame 5 is filled in as a solid bright disc.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the four distant players across the court (roughly 9–14 m from the camera wearer) and the camera wearer's foreground racket (roughly 0.5–0.8 m away at the bottom edge, labeled 'tennis racket' in frames 3 and 5). On the left side of the court, two players stand roughly 2–4 m apart at 10–14 m distance, with the inner player in a light-blue shirt moving rightward to pass behind the net post in frame 4 and crouch behind the net in frame 5. On the right side at 9–12 m distance, two players (one in red, one in dark clothing) converge until they stand within arm's reach of each other (less than 0.5 m apart), mutually occluding into a single merged 'person' mask in frames 2 and 3 before separating into two adjacent masks in frames 4 and 5. This map highlights individual player instances and separates the overlapping pair on the right in frames 1, 4, and 5 more distinctly than a quick glance at the wide-angle RGB strip. However, it is unreliable in several places: it fails to detect the motion-blurred foreground racket in frame 1 and its rim at the bottom of frames 2 and 4, misclassifies the net base as a 'skateboard' and the basketball hoop support as a 'person' in frame 2, labels a ceiling duct as a 'person' in frame 3, and hallucinates a large 'train' mask across the upper walls and balcony in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, containing no body or hand skeleton detections anywhere in the scene. From the RGB context, four people are present at roughly 9–14 m in front of the camera wearer—two on the left side of the net oriented mostly toward the net and right court, and two on the right side who turn toward each other and stand within arm's reach, with none directly facing or looking at the camera wearer—while the camera wearer's own hand holding the racket remains cropped out below the bottom edge of the frame. Because the map is entirely empty, it provides no spatial information about body orientation, gaze direction, limb articulation, or reach across the sequence, and adds nothing beyond the RGB strip. It is completely unreliable here because the distant players occupy too few pixels in the wide-angle view for skeleton extraction and the camera wearer's hands remain outside the field of view.
